issues.description: The problem statement requires an instance method swiftExperienceDescription() that returns a String and whose result should be printed from the initializer (the method is intended to produce a String to be printed). The template, however, already defines a method with the same name but with no return type (void) and which prints directly (func swiftExperienceDescription() { print("") }). In Swift you cannot overload a function only by return type, so students cannot implement the required swiftExperienceDescription() -> String without modifying the template's existing method. This also conflicts with the initializer TODO which expects to call the method and print its returned String. The solution implements swiftExperienceDescription() -> String, matching the problem statement.
issues.suggested_fix: Update the template so the extension declares swiftExperienceDescription() with the correct signature and semantics: func swiftExperienceDescription() -> String { ... } (returning the description instead of printing). In the initializer TODO, call and print its result (print(self.swiftExperienceDescription())). This aligns the template with the problem statement and the solution, and avoids a blocking name/signature conflict for students.
